Here’s a factual research note on the claim “Over 23,000 hectares of forest restored in Yugra” (Ханты-Мансийский автономный округ — Югра), based on live sources as of late November 2026:

---

## What the Claim Is

The story reports that **over 23,000 hectares** of forest have been restored in Yugra in 2026. Key details include:

- Restoration took place **on forest fund lands** between **May and early November** 2026 under the federal project *“Сохранение лесов”* (“Forest Conservation”) of the national project *“Ecological Well-Being”*. ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  
- Of the total area restored, **20,000 hectares** recovered naturally; an additional **3,200 hectares** were reforested artificially. ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  
- The “balance of loss and reproduction” of forests in the region was reported at **115%**, meaning that more area was restored than was lost (by harvesting, fire, disease, etc.). ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  
- Some local breakdowns:  
  - **Самаровское лесничество** (Samarovskoye forest district): over **11,000 hectares** restored.  
  - **Советское лесничество** (Sovetskoye): about **4,000 hectares**.  
  - **Октябрьское лесничество** (Oktyabrskoye): about **1,600 hectares**. ([sitv.ru](https://sitv.ru/arhiv/news/bolee-23-tysyach-gektarov-lesa-vosstanovili-v-yugre-za-god/?utm_source=openai))  

Also noted:  
- Spring 2026: over **21,000 trees** planted as part of the “Сад памяти” (“Memory Garden”) campaign.  
- Autumn 2026: over **5 million seedlings** planted in a “Сохраним лес” (“Let’s Save the Forest”) action involving forestry specialists, leaseholders, and mineral resource users. ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Sources and Their Type

- The primary source appears to be a **press release** by the *Департамент недропользования и природных ресурсов Югры* (Department of Subsoil Use and Natural Resources of Yugra), shared via their official MAX messenger channel. ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  
- Independent regional media, e.g. *Surgut Inform-TV / Новости Сургута* (“News of Surgut­TV”) have reported the same numbers, citing statements from the same regional department and officials. ([sitv.ru](https://sitv.ru/arhiv/news/bolee-23-tysyach-gektarov-lesa-vosstanovili-v-yugre-za-god/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed/Measured Outcomes vs. Plans or Pledges

These are **measured outcomes** (i.e. what has actually been completed), not just plans or projections, as of the reporting date:

- The restoration work up to early November 2026 (and seasonal actions) is described in past tense: “restored …”, “renewed …”. ([sitv.ru](https://sitv.ru/arhiv/news/bolee-23-tysyach-gektarov-lesa-vosstanovili-v-yugre-za-god/?utm_source=openai))  
- Specific hectares are given as achieved (e.g. 20,000 natural + 3,200 artificial = ~23,200 hectares). ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Additional Context That Contrasts With the Claim

- Earlier in 2026 (September), Yugra had **planned** to restore about **20,100 hectares** (13,000 natural, 7,000 artificial). That was a target under the same programs. ([ugra.aif.ru](https://ugra.aif.ru/incidents/v-yugre-vosstanovyat-bolee-20-tysyach-gektarov-lesa?from_inject=1&utm_source=openai))  
- For **2025**, Yugra had restored over **26,000 hectares** of forest, exceeding targets. ([ugra-news.ru](https://ugra-news.ru/article/v_2025_godu_v_yugre_vosstanovili_bolee_26_tysyach_gektarov_lesa/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Why Some Version Discrepancies Appear

- The **23,000+ hectares** figure refers specifically to work done **between May and early November 2026**, i.e. a subset of the year. It is a **partial‐year result**, not the full‐year outcome. ([max.ru](https://max.ru/depnedraugra/AaIbMil4UC4?utm_source=openai))  
- Earlier reports of targets/plans are used by some outlets (e.g. “restore over 20,000 hectares in 2026”) which are planning data. ([ugra.aif.ru](https://ugra.aif.ru/incidents/v-yugre-vosstanovyat-bolee-20-tysyach-gektarov-lesa?from_inject=1&utm_source=openai))  

---

## Verification Status & Reliability

- The numbers are reported by the official regional department; there is **no independent scientific verification** cited in these sources, such as satellite imagery or audited field data, beyond the government's internal reporting.  
- Media reports largely **repeat the department’s press release**; they do not appear to supply additional sources or challenge the claim.  

---

## Summary: What Actually Happened

- As of **late November 2026**, Yugra has **restored over 23,000 hectares** of forest on forest fund lands, during forestry activities under national/federal projects.  
- Of that, approx. **20,000 ha** were restored **naturally**, and **3,200 ha** through **artificial planting**.  
- The restoration amount **exceeds** loss (harvest, damage, etc.) by 15% (i.e. balance of reproduction is 115%).  
- The season of restoration was roughly **May to early November 2026**, with major citizen involvement in tree planting campaigns.  

---

If you like, I can try to locate independent environmental or scientific confirmations (e.g. satellite or NGO reports) to cross-check these claims.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a research-note on the candidate event (“Community clinic use rose and patient burden declined in China”) based on available evidence. I found no support for that claim in high-quality, original sources; in fact, most recent data point in the opposite direction.

---

## What I looked for

- Any recent peer-reviewed or official data showing *increased* use of community clinics (or primary care) in China  
- Evidence that patient burden (financial, travel, or other access burden) has *declined*  

---

## Key related studies & findings

1. **China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), 2012-2022**  
   - A longitudinal study of Chinese adults’ *usual source of care*. Measures whether people primarily use primary care, clinics, or hospitals. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42287038/?utm_source=openai))  
   - *Findings:* From 2012 to 2022, the proportion using primary care as their usual source **declined** from ~43.5 % to ~30.3 %, while hospital share **rose** from ~34.1 % to ~46.8 %.  
   - Inflows into primary care (people starting to use it) dropped; outflows (people leaving primary care) increased. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42287038/?utm_source=openai))  

   — This strongly contradicts “community clinic use rose.”

2. **Village clinics in rural China (2011-2018)**  
   - A nationally representative panel study of rural households and village clinics, with decomposition analysis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10266832/?utm_source=openai))  
   - *Findings:* Use of village clinics when ill **fell by 44 %** over this period. Outpatient services in county hospitals increased (~56 %), and self-treatment rose (~20 %). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10266832/?utm_source=openai))  

   — Again, the trend is away from lower-level community/village clinics, not toward them.

3. **Equality & unmet needs (1993-2018)**  
   - Household surveys (National Health Service Survey) track outpatient visits, hospital admissions, unmet needs due to financial burden, across urban/rural and income groups. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10204261/?utm_source=openai))  
   - *Findings:* Overall outpatient visit rate dropped then recovered; hospitalizations increased; financial burden-related unmet need *declined*, as did unmet admission needs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10204261/?utm_source=openai))  

   — This indicates some reduction in “patient burden” (in terms of unable to afford treatment or unable to be admitted) over decades, but doesn’t clearly link to an increase in community clinic use.

4. **Recent data from Henan Province (2014-2024)**  
   - Time-series study examining recovery after COVID-19 disruptions. Looks at hospital vs township health centres (THCs) in outpatient visits. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/public-health/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1916015/full?utm_source=openai))  
   - *Findings:* After COVID-19 restrictions eased, visits to township health centres significantly exceeded what would have been expected (~39-40 % higher than baseline in 2024), while hospital visits remained below expected levels. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/public-health/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1916015/full?utm_source=openai))  

   — This suggests *increase* in use of primary-level THCs post-COVID in Henan, but measured relative to expected trends: it’s a partial recovery / upward shift, not necessarily a sustained nationwide “community clinic use rose” over long term, nor firm evidence of broadly declined burden.

---

## Assessment of the claim

- The summary “Community clinic use rose and patient burden declined in China” is **not supported** by the major recent national studies. The strongest longitudinal data (CFPS, village clinics studies) show **declines** in primary care or community clinic usage from lower-level clinics, with shifting toward hospitals or self-treatment.  
- “Patient burden” (especially financial unmet needs) has declined over longer periods (1990s-2018), particularly for hospital admissions, but evidence is mixed and often not specific to community clinics.  
- More recent, more localized data (e.g. in Henan Province post-COVID) do show township health center visits exceeding expected levels, hinting at increased primary care use locally. But that’s not equivalent to national reversal of the overall decline.  

---

## Conclusion

- **What actually seems to have happened:** In China, usage of lower-level/community/village clinics has generally *decreased* over roughly the past decade (e.g. 2011–2018; 2012–2022), with more people using hospitals or opting for self-treatment.  
- Patient burden in terms of financial barriers and unmet needs has *decreased* over longer time-spans (1990s-2018) but with variation, and not necessarily directly tied to increased community clinic usage.

- **What has *not* been demonstrated in reliable sources:** A national trend showing *community clinic use rose* in recent years, and that this rise has directly caused a *decline in patient burden.*

---

If you want, I can try to find whether there is *any* credible recent evidence (2024–2026) that matches the claim more closely (community clinic usage up + patient burden reducing), in which case it might be more localized or policy specific. Do you want me to dig for that?

stories.research_notes:
Here’s a **research note** on the claim **“Biomes restoration in Brazil increases by 231.6% in five years”**, based on recent data. I have identified the primary source, verified actual outcomes vs. launch/plans, and noted which parts are new measured data vs. updated/mapped data.

---

### Key Finding (Measured Outcome)

- According to the **Observatório da Restauração (OR)**, under the *Coalizão Brasil Clima, Florestas e Agricultura*, Brazil’s mapped area of **native vegetation restoration in progress** rose from approximately **79,000 hectares in 2021** to **262,000 hectares in 2026**. That is an increase of **231.6%** over five years. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))

- From 2025 to 2026 specifically, the mapped area grew by **58,300 hectares**, a year-over-year increase of **29%**. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))

---

### Source & Credibility

- **Primary Source**: The data comes from the **Observatório da Restauração (OR)**, from its **fourth edition**, published in **November 2026**. The OR is part of the **Coalizão Brasil Clima, Florestas e Agricultura**. ([exame.com](https://exame.com/esg/brasil-triplica-area-de-restauracao-florestal-e-novo-programa-mira-r-220-milhoes/?utm_source=openai))

- The Coalizão website corroborates this, stating: *“Restauração no Brasil: área mapeada mais do que triplica em cinco anos e chega a 262 mil hectares”*. ([coalizaobr.com.br](https://coalizaobr.com.br/?utm_source=openai))

---

### Additional Context & Breakdown

- **By biome**:
  - *Mata Atlântica* leads in total area: **153,700 hectares**, about **58.7%** of Brazil’s total restoration efforts in this dataset. It increased by **22,800 hectares** (17%) from 2025 to 2026. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))
  - *Amazônia* saw the fastest relative annual gain: **61%** increase in one year (39,600 → 63,800 hectares). ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))
  - *Cerrado* increased by 35% year-over-year, from 31,600 to 42,800 hectares. ([boca.com.br](https://boca.com.br/meio-ambiente/area-de-restauracao-no-brasil-cresce-2316-em-cinco-anos?utm_source=openai))
  - *Caatinga, Pantanal and Pampa* together account for **less than 1%** of the mapped restoration area; the study attributes this mainly to *lack of available data* in those biomes. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))

- **Restoration techniques & participation**:
  - *Regeneração natural* (natural regeneration) is used in **46%** of all the mapped restoration area (~121,000 ha), and is especially predominant in the Amazon (73% there). ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))
  - Other techniques: *isolation* (blocking grazing, fire etc.), *plantio em área total* (full planting), etc. Distribution varies by biome & land type—e.g., in property lands vs. conservation units. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))

- **Actors involved**:
  - **Society civil** manages 90% of the mapped areas; executes 41% of projects. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))
  - **Public sector** finances 52% of areas; **private sector** finances 22% of areas but executes 30%. ([observatoriosergipe.com.br](https://observatoriosergipe.com.br/noticias/areas-em-restauracao-no-brasil-crescem-231-6-em-cinco-anos-aponta-levantamento-f077bc2c1ae1?utm_source=openai))

---

### Caveats & Interpretations

- The increase refers to **mapped & registered restoration efforts**, not necessarily the total actual restoration happening. The report notes that *some of the increase is due to projects that were already ongoing but had not been included in the previous mapping/database*. ([tmc.com.br](https://tmc.com.br/brasil/restauracao-de-biomas-no-brasil-mais-do-que-triplica-em-cinco-anos/?utm_source=openai))

- The data does **not measure** outcomes in terms of ecological health, carbon capture, or biodiversity improvements—just the spatial extent of areas in restoration *process*.

- Some geographic coverage is inconsistent—biomes like Caatinga, Pantanal and Pampa are underrepresented due to limited data availability. This suggests the totals might undercount actual restoration in those biomes. ([observatoriosergipe.com.br](https://observatoriosergipe.com.br/noticias/areas-em-restauracao-no-brasil-crescem-231-6-em-cinco-anos-aponta-levantamento-f077bc2c1ae1?utm_source=openai))

---

### Independent Reporting & Confirmation

- Multiple independent media outlets (e.g., *Exame*, *Agência Brasil*) have reported these figures, largely repeating the data provided by the OR and the Coalizão. ([exame.com](https://exame.com/esg/brasil-triplica-area-de-restauracao-florestal-e-novo-programa-mira-r-220-milhoes/?utm_source=openai))

- No contradictory data found to contradict the claim of 231.6%; no clear independent scientific peer-reviewed source yet provides alternative numbers that differ.

---

### Summary

- **What happened**: The area of **registered native vegetation restoration in Brazil** rose by ~231.6% from 2021 to 2026, according to the latest measured data by the OR/Coalizão Brasil. The mapped area increased from ~79,000 to ~262,000 hectares.

- **Verified?** Yes—based on OR’s national mapping and reporting.

- **Is this completed restoration?** No—these are restoration *in process*; outcome metrics (e.g. biodiversity, carbon, maturity of vegetation) are not part of the metric reported.

- **Announcement vs reality**: These are measured figures, not just a pledge. They reflect what has been documented on the ground (or via mapping/data collection), as of 2026.

---

### Implications (not evaluative, but factual)

- Brazil is showing measurable growth in its restoration efforts, especially in Mata Atlântica and Amazônia biomes.

- The reported increase helps monitor progress toward national/international environmental goals (e.g., Brazil’s restoration / deforestation commitments).

- Gaps remain in data coverage (certain biomes underrepresented), and the fact that part of the increase comes from retrospective inclusion of older projects means that part of the growth is by updating the database, not only by new restoration activity.

---

If you like, I can pull up the original OR report in full, with charts, dates, biogeographic maps, etc., to visualize how restoration is distributed.

**Research note — correction:** The event appears to be the **temporary reopening of the Danube navigation channel near Paks**, not a reopening after flooding. The reported closure had lasted more than three months and was due to construction of a riverbed sill and unusually low water levels. An official navigation notice set a temporary traffic regime through **December 5, 2026**; independent Hungarian reporting says the temporary channel was **60 metres wide**, with downstream traffic starting **November 25** and two-way traffic allowed from **November 26**. More than 80 vessels were waiting to pass. ([pannonris.hu](https://pannonris.hu/pdf/117_Du_2026?utm_source=openai))

This was a **limited, temporary reopening**, not yet the full-width channel reopening: the water authority was reported as expecting to seek that around **December 20**, after construction. The claim that resumed shipping was aiding flood victims is unsupported by the sources reviewed; they describe drought/low water and construction, not flooding or flood recovery. ([24.hu](https://24.hu/tudomany/2026/11/27/duna-paks-jarhato-fenekkuszob-hajozas/?utm_source=openai))

**Source note:** Several reports attribute their details to the same Hungarian water-authority announcement or the transport minister’s social-media post, so they should not be treated as separate confirmations. ([iho.hu](https://iho.hu/hirek/ujra-lehet-hajozni-a-dunan-paksnal-261126?utm_source=openai))

stories.research_notes:
Here is a fact-check research note on the event “WSSC lifts water conservation request for Montgomery, Prince George’s counties,” based on original and secondary sources:

---

## What Happened

- **Utility involved**: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC Water), which provides drinking water to 1.9 million customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties in Maryland. ([wsscwater.com](https://www.wsscwater.com/news/2026/november/final-update-830-am-friday-november-27-2026-essential-water-use-only-request?utm_source=openai))  
- **The issue**: A major storm (Thanksgiving nor’easter) caused intermittent power disruptions at WSSC’s two water filtration plants—Potomac and Patuxent. ([baltimorechronicle.com](https://baltimorechronicle.com/baltimore/wssc-water-essential-use-only-request/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Resulting action**: WSSC issued an “Essential Water Use Only” request at **2:30 PM on Thursday, November 26, 2026**, asking customers to sharply curtail water use (for example, avoid outdoor water use, limit dishwashing, laundry, toilet flushing) as a precaution while power was disrupted. Drinking water remained safe; no boil-water advisory was issued. ([world-today-journal.com](https://world-today-journal.com/wssc-water-conservation-request-use-water-only-for-essentials-until-power-stabilizes/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Outcome / Resolution

- **Lifting of the request**: The “Essential Water Use Only” request was lifted at **8:30 AM on Friday, November 27, 2026**. The request affected all 1.9 million WSSC customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties. ([wsscwater.com](https://www.wsscwater.com/news/2026/november/final-update-830-am-friday-november-27-2026-essential-water-use-only-request?utm_source=openai))  
- **System status when lifted**: Both water filtration plants (Potomac and Patuxent) were producing safe, clean drinking water. The water treatment and distribution systems were operating normally. WSSC also noted that disruptions from the storm had diminished. ([wsscwater.com](https://www.wsscwater.com/news/2026/november/final-update-830-am-friday-november-27-2026-essential-water-use-only-request?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Sources & Verification

- **Original / primary source**: WSSC’s own press release titled “Final Update – 8:30 a.m. Friday, November 27, 2026: Essential Water Use Only Request Lifted” from their official website. ([wsscwater.com](https://www.wsscwater.com/news/2026/november/final-update-830-am-friday-november-27-2026-essential-water-use-only-request?utm_source=openai))

- **Independent reporting**: The Banner (regional news outlet) and NBC Washington both reported the lifting of the advisory, quoting WSSC and confirming the 8:30 AM time and 1.9 million customers affected. ([thebanner.com](https://www.thebanner.com/community/local-news/wssc-water-essential-water-request-storm-5TL6JWNZLBFT7NXXRMJVBKCW3Y/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completeness & Context

- **Completed outcome**: Yes — the conservation request was lifted; there is a measurable resolution. City operations returned to normal water production and distribution.  
- **What remains unknown**: No further forecast of possible renewed advisory (if power were to become unstable again), though WSSC said it would continue monitoring. ([baltimorechronicle.com](https://baltimorechronicle.com/baltimore/wssc-water-essential-use-only-request/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Summary

WSSC’s “Essential Water Use Only” request for Montgomery and Prince George’s counties—initially issued Thursday afternoon (November 26, 2026) due to storm-related power disruptions at major filtration plants—was lifted early the next morning (8:30 AM, Friday, November 27). The request had affected 1.9 million customers; by the time of lifting, both plants were operating normally, water production met demand, and the distribution system was restored. Drinking water remained safe; there was no boil-water advisory. The event is fully completed.
